articles.title: How to Test JWT Authentication and Silent Token Refresh in React Without a Backend
articles.excerpt: I once lost an entire Saturday afternoon trying to debug a silent JWT token refresh loop in a React app I was building. The login modal and user dashboard were completely done. But testing the actual…
articles.body: I once lost an entire Saturday afternoon trying to debug a silent JWT token refresh loop in a React app I was building. The login modal and user dashboard were completely done. But testing the actual security mechanics was driving me up the wall: How was I supposed to test what happens when an access token expires after 15 minutes? How could I verify that my Axios interceptor cleanly caught the 401 Unauthorized , paused queued requests, called /auth/refresh , and retried the original request without logging the user out? How could I test updating authenticated profile data via PATCH /auth/me ? The backend team wasn't ready yet, and none of the public mock APIs in the ecosystem offered realistic JWT authentication.
articles.author: Nilesh Kumar

I wanted the opposite: a generator that's free, private by default, and natively callable by AI agents. So I built FreeQrly — open source ( BryceBin/freeqrly , MIT), running entirely on Cloudflare Pages + D1. Here's the architecture, including the part I think is most interesting: one shared auth/quota core serving three surfaces — web UI, REST API, and MCP. The three surfaces 1. articles.body: 탈중앙화되고 안전하며 불변하는 원장이라는 블록체인 기술의 근본적인 약속은 지난 10년 넘게 기술자와 경제학자 모두를 사로잡았다. 하지만 이 산업이 단순한 개념을 넘어 실제 애플리케이션으로 성숙해지면서, "블록체인 트릴레마"라 불리는 근본적인 설계 제약이 핵심 과제로 떠올랐다. 이 트릴레마는 블록체인 시스템이 확장성, 보안, 탈중앙화라는 세 가지 바람직한 속성 중 어느 한 시점에 오직 두 가지만 최적으로 달성할 수 있다고 말한다. 이러한 본질적인 상충관계는 블록체인 공간의 거의 모든 아키텍처 결정과 지속적인 혁신의 기반을 이룬다. 수년간 비트코인이나 초기 이더리움 같은 블록체인 네트워크는 보안과 탈중앙화를 우선시하며 공격과 검열에 대한 강력한 저항력을 확보했다. 하지만 이는 제한된 트랜잭션 처리량이라는 대가를 치렀다. 네트워크 수요가 급증하는 시기에 이러한 한계는 더욱 명확해졌고, 엄청난 트랜잭션 수수료와 느린 확인 시간으로 이어져 높은 트랜잭션 볼륨을 요구하는 애플리케이션의 주류 채택을 가로막았다. 이 트릴레마를 해결하는 것은 단순히 학술적인 과제가 아니다. 이는 블록체인을 틈새 기술에서 벗어나 글로벌 금융 시스템, 공급망, 그리고 급성장하는 웹3(Web3) 애플리케이션을 지원할 수 있는 보편적인 인프라로 전환하기 위한 필수적인 단계다. 이 글은 블록체인 트릴레마의 복잡한 면모를 깊이 파고들어, 그 영향을 완화하기 위해 사용된 다양한 기술 전략들을 탐색하고, 실제 구현 사례들을 분석하며, 탈중앙화 네트워크의 미래를 계속 형성하고 있는 내재된 한계들을 논의할 것이다.

articles.title: Browser-First Tools Are Quietly Replacing Bloated SaaS Apps
articles.excerpt: I have a small test I use before installing another productivity app: does this task actually need a server? A lot of everyday work fails that test. Renaming a batch of files, counting words, formatti…
articles.body: I have a small test I use before installing another productivity app: does this task actually need a server? A lot of everyday work fails that test. Renaming a batch of files, counting words, formatting JSON, removing blank lines from a draft, compressing one image, or merging two PDFs does not require an account, a sync engine, a monthly subscription, or a copy of the file sitting in someone else's storage. Yet those are exactly the tasks that often get wrapped in a full SaaS product. The result is familiar: a 2 MB task comes with a 40 MB interface. You sign up, verify an email, pick a plan, upload a file, wait for a spinner, download the result, and then wonder why the whole thing needed a cloud. Browser-first tools are not a universal replacement for SaaS.

articles.title: I Built a Client-Side Favicon Generator (60-Second Tutorial)
articles.excerpt: Your logo looks great at 1200px. At 16x16, it's a smudge. That's the entire favicon problem in one sentence. Every site needs that tiny tab icon, and the standard workflow for making one is embarrassi…
articles.body: Your logo looks great at 1200px. At 16x16, it's a smudge. That's the entire favicon problem in one sentence. Every site needs that tiny tab icon, and the standard workflow for making one is embarrassingly bad: upload your logo to some generator, create an account, wait in a queue, download a watermarked PNG, realize it's a single 32px file with no ICO, no Apple touch icon, no manifest — and start over. I got tired of that loop, so I built a favicon generator that runs 100% in the browser: type 1–3 initials or pick an emoji, set colors, preview at real tab sizes, and download the full pack (ICO, PNGs, Apple touch icons, PWA manifest). No upload, no signup, no watermark. This post is the 60-second tutorial plus the one canvas technique that makes it all work. The 60-second workflow 1.

articles.title: SUMIF vs SUMIFS vs COUNTIFS: which Excel function to use when
articles.excerpt: Excel has a whole family of "add this up, but only for some rows" functions, and their names look almost identical. The rule that sorts them out is short: IF means one condition, IFS means several. Th…
articles.body: Excel has a whole family of "add this up, but only for some rows" functions, and their names look almost identical. The rule that sorts them out is short: IF means one condition, IFS means several. The rest is remembering which argument goes first. TL;DR: one condition → SUMIF / COUNTIF / AVERAGEIF ; more than one → SUMIFS / COUNTIFS ; just count non-empty cells → COUNTA . The examples below use a staff sheet with 25 people in rows 2 to 26: column A is the name, B the department, C the office, D the sales figure. We ran each formula on that sheet in Excel for the web. The functions, one by one SUMIF: add with one condition. =SUMIF(B2:B26,"Sales",D2:D26) adds column D only where the department is "Sales". Order: where to check, what to match, what to add.

articles.excerpt: From start to finish, these 10 NES games reward every second of the time you invest in them, even decades after the fact.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1985, Nintendo released the Nintendo Entertainment System in North America alongside a limited selection of games like Super Mario Bros. and Excitebike . Within a few years, it had a library of hundreds of titles, proving that rumors of the video game industry’s death throughout the early ‘80s were greatly exaggerated. Today, many of those early games feel like antiques. They’re not nearly as memorable as they once were, with so many generations of newer software to choose from. But there are some that still deserve your attention, even now. Here are 10 NES games that are still worth playing from start to finish.

articles.title: 9 Best DLCs That Were Even Better Than the Base Game
articles.excerpt: From Hell weddings to alien hive-minds, these nine DLCs took a hard swerve away from the games they built off.
articles.body: Even the wildest DLC needs a solid game to swerve away from, or the swerve doesn’t land. Every base game with excellent DLC is strong enough to stand on its own. That’s the common DNA: studios that had built something sturdy enough to trust it, confident enough to hand players a portal to hell, an alien hive-mind under a suburban cul-de-sac, or a crown that makes you ruler of an entire realm of madness — and bet that players would play anyway. For these nine DLCs, that confidence turned out to be well-placed. Here are the best DLCs of all time that took their main story and had the confidence to dream up wild new experiences for dedicated players. Each of these nine game expansions took a big swing, and has been remembered for that creativity ever since.

articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.excerpt: From the Costa del Sol to whitewashed mountain villages, here are 10 of the best places in southern Spain to experience the Aug. 2, 2027 total solar eclipse.
articles.body: Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East. However, choosing where to watch requires some thought.

articles.excerpt: The Artemis II crew have joined an impressive list of honourees, including Buzz Aldrin, Jane Goodall and David Attenborough.
articles.body: TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure. Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover , alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen , accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch , who wasn't in attendance.

The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
